source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: BenchBase (benchbase at commit 33c00473807ebd49304d114a6d769d2d2b2bbb34), benchmark auctionmark, generated into SQLite at scale factor 1 (config/sqlite/sample_auctionmark_config.xml with <scalefactor>1</scalefactor> instead of the sample's 0.1; the DDL BenchBase applies for SQLite is ddl-generic.sql, whose column names are those of ddl-postgres.sql), every table exported to benchbase/auctionmark/<table>.csv with the DDL column names: item (root) left-joined to useracct on i_u_id = u_id, useracct to region on u_r_id = r_id, item to category on i_c_id = c_id, and category to itself twice along c_parent_id = c_id (roles parent and grandparent; a NULL c_parent_id keeps empty parent columns); dropped the free-text columns i_description and i_user_attributes, the filler attributes i_iattr0-7, u_sattr0-7 and u_iattr0-7, the timestamps i_created, i_updated and u_updated, the counters i_num_global_attrs and u_comments, and the ids u_id, r_id and c_id of the joined tables, which equal the join columns; timestamps are relative to the load time, so the generated database is kept as the snapshot.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE item: "PRIMARY KEY (i_id, i_u_id)"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-postgres.sql, CREATE TABLE item: "PRIMARY KEY (i_id, i_u_id)"
truth.justification: (i_id, i_u_id) is the declared primary key of item, and the right-hand side are columns of item.

truth.justification: i_u_id (the seller) references the declared primary key u_id of useracct, so it identifies one useracct row and its columns.

truth.clause: benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE item: "i_c_id              BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES category (c_id)"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE category: "PRIMARY KEY (c_id)"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-postgres.sql, CREATE TABLE item: "FOREIGN KEY (i_c_id) REFERENCES category (c_id) ON DELETE CASCADE"
truth.justification: i_c_id references the declared primary key c_id of category, so it identifies one category row (the item's category) and its name and parent.

truth.clause: benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE category: "c_parent_id         BIGINT REFERENCES category (c_id)" and "PRIMARY KEY (c_id)"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-postgres.sql, CREATE TABLE category: "FOREIGN KEY (c_parent_id) REFERENCES category (c_id) ON DELETE CASCADE"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, comment of CATEGORY: "Category can be hierarchical aligned using c_parent_id."
truth.justification: c_parent_id references the declared primary key of category itself, so a non-null value identifies one parent row; c_parent_id is nullable (no NOT NULL), a top-level category has no parent row and keeps empty parent columns, which does not break the dependency.

audit.quote: c_parent_id BIGINT REFERENCES category (c_id) ‖ FOREIGN KEY (c_parent_id) REFERENCES category (c_id) ON DELETE CASCADE ‖ PRIMARY KEY (c_id) ‖ Category can be hierarchical aligned using c_parent_id.

truth.clause: benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE category: "c_parent_id         BIGINT REFERENCES category (c_id)" and "PRIMARY KEY (c_id)"; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-postgres.sql, CREATE TABLE category: "FOREIGN KEY (c_parent_id) REFERENCES category (c_id) ON DELETE CASCADE"
truth.justification: The same self-reference one level up: the parent's c_parent_id identifies one grandparent row; empty when the parent is top-level or absent.

audit.quote: c_parent_id BIGINT REFERENCES category (c_id) ‖ FOREIGN KEY (c_parent_id) REFERENCES category (c_id) ON DELETE CASCADE ‖ PRIMARY KEY (c_id)

truth.clause: hstore_projects_auctionmark.html, 2.3.1 ITEM: "The ITEM id consists of a composite key where the lower 48-bits of the number is the USER.u id and the upper 16-bits is the auction count for that user."; benchbase_auctionmark_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE item: "i_id                VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL" and "PRIMARY KEY (i_id, i_u_id)"
truth.justification: Unsure: the H-Store page states that the item id embeds the seller id, which makes i_id alone identify the seller; this is stated for the 64-bit ids of the H-Store implementation and not confirmed for the BenchBase port, whose pinned DDL types i_id as VARCHAR(128) and declares the composite primary key (i_id, i_u_id) without contradicting the statement.

audit.quote: The ITEM id consists of a composite key where the lower 48-bits of the number is the USER.u id and the upper 16-bits is the auction count for that user. ‖ i_id BIGINT ‖ i_id VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL ‖ PRIMARY KEY (i_id, i_u_id)

gold_design_note: No normalized design is published; the 3NF designs of Sigma* are synthesized.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
